🚨🌍 <u>IRAN SHUTS THE STRAIT OF HORMUZ AFTER US STRIKES HORMOZGAN</u>

Iran's Revolutionary Guard declared the Strait of Hormuz "closed to traffic of any type of vessel" — tankers and merchant ships included — after CENTCOM struck targets in Hormozgan province. Any ship that tries to pass will be attacked. Roughly 20% of the world's oil moves through this 39-km chokepoint.

The Pentagon picked the fight. Tehran picked the terrain.

🇲🇽🏭 <u>ROCÍO NAHLE — VERACRUZ GOVERNOR — RANKS TOP 10 NATIONALLY AT 65.9%</u>

Demoscopia Digital ranks Rocío Nahle 7th among Mexico's 32 governors at 65.9% approval — her highest reading since December 2024, up from 63.2%. The architect of the Dos Bocas refinery now governs the state that holds the bulk of Pemex's strategic fields, with rising marks for managing state finances and social programs.

The right wing said she'd fail. Veracruz says otherwise.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>TELEVISA INVITED THE SUPREME COURT TO ITS AZTECA STADIUM PALCO</u>

Televisa executives invited Mexico's Supreme Court justices to the World Cup opener at the Azteca. Seven declined, citing conflict of interest. Justices Yasmín Esquivel and Giovanni Figueroa confirmed they're going. In March the Court ruled 6-to-let Televisa pocket a 103-million-peso tax refund.

The palco isn't a gift. It's a receipt.

🚨🇨🇺 <u>HEGSETH FLIES TO GUANTÁNAMO TO THREATEN CUBA OVER WEAPONS</u>

US "Secretary of War" Pete Hegseth — yes, that's the official Pentagon title now — traveled to the Guantánamo Naval Base to warn Havana not to acquire weapons that could "threaten" US territory. The visit comes as Washington tightens sanctions on Cuban leaders and chokes the island's oil supply.

A threat issued from the base the US has refused to return for 122 years, on the island it has blockaded for 64.

🚨🇨🇺 <u>US WAGES AI PSYCHOLOGICAL WAR ON CUBA — HAVANA</u>

Cuba's Foreign Ministry says Washington is now running AI-generated psychological warfare against the island — synthetic content, fabricated voices, manufactured narratives — to engineer collapse while the oil blockade strangles the grid. FM Bruno Rodríguez called the blackouts not a product of government negligence but of the U.S. "atrocious war" and sanctions.

The 1962 embargo never ended. It just learned to code.

CBP: Mexico cooperates more than ever on border security — Commissioner Rodney Scott
June 10, 2026 | 🟢

📰 US Border Patrol commissioner Rodney Scott tells the Center for Immigration Studies in DC that US-Mexico cooperation is at "one of its best moments." Direct contradiction of the WSJ, National Review, and Washington Examiner opinion lanes still running "Sheinbaum protects narco-politicians."

The enforcement agencies say one thing; the opinion pages say another. Worth noting which one US media amplifies.

• "We are sharing information in a way we have never done before"
• "and we are actually getting results" — Rodney Scott, CBP Commissioner

AL JAZEERA: Mexico braces for celebrations, protests as World Cup opens amid tensions
June 11, 2026 | 🟢

📰 Same AP wire base, but Al Jazeera lets the body breathe — CNTE teachers and 133,000 missing persons treated as substantive crises, not optics problems. Sheinbaum quoted matter-of-factly: if the Zócalo can't be used, "there are 18 venues" ready.

Absent here: the US-press tic of treating Mexican protest as proof of state failure.

• "They should be investing in education … not giving the city a makeover"
• "You can see a lot more police on the streets, and there is a sense that there [is safety]" — resident

AP/WAPO: Celebrations clash with social tensions in Mexico on the eve of the World Cup
June 10, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Megan Janetsky's AP wire has Sheinbaum "walking a political tightrope" the day before her country hosts the world. The body of the piece actually carries the CNTE teacher and disappeared-families demands seriously; the headline frames it as "clash."

100,000 security personnel deployed, ~$3B expected economic impact — both numbers reported, neither in headline.

• "Mexico wants to project an image to the world that doesn't exactly square with reality" — analyst Carlos Pérez Ricart
• "Everything is under control" — Sheinbaum
• "They should be investing in education, not giving the city a makeover" — protest organizer

WSJ: World Cup Puts Mexico's Cartel Crisis on the Global Stage
June 11, 2026 | 🔴

📰 WSJ frames the tournament itself as the exposure event — not a sporting moment, but a stage where Mexico's "cartel crisis" gets performed for the world. The 100,000-personnel security operation (Plan Kukulkan) doesn't register in the headline.

(Paywalled — analysis based on headline + visible framing.)
